subject: Recap + parity probes for MedSync vendor comparison

Subject: Recap + parity probes for MedSync vendor comparison

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap to make sure we captured the pain, the goals, and the set of parity probes that will help MedSync decide between Redwood and the other vendors in your bake-off. I summarized below and proposed concrete, runnable probes so your engineering team can validate the behaviors that matter most.

Top pain points you shared:
- High per-request cost at scale for long-context transcriptions (typical sessions ~600–1,200 tokens).
- Latency spikes that affect clinician UI when multiple requests are concurrent.
- Need for deterministic behavior on structured outputs (SOAP-like notes) for downstream parsers.
- Visibility/audit requirements: token-level cost breakdown and request audit logs for compliance.

Primary goals for evaluation (decision criteria):
1) End-to-end latency P95 for a 512-token generation under 350ms (region: us-west).
2) Cost per 1k tokens at production batch sizes <= 45% of current baseline.
3) Output stability — <5% semantic divergence across repeated prompts + fixed seed.
4) Operational telemetry & auditability: per-request trace, token accounting, and KV-cache hit metrics.

Suggested parity probes (what to run / acceptance criteria):
- Probe A — Long-context parity: 1,000-token prompt + 300-token generation. Measure P50/P95 latency and tokens/sec. Accept if P95 <= 600ms and throughput >= X tokens/sec (we'll provide measurement harness).
- Probe B — Concurrency ramp: 1–64 simultaneous 512-token requests. Capture latency tail and error rates; pass if error rate < 0.5% and P95 increase <= 2x from single-client baseline.
- Probe C — Structured extraction stability: run 200 repeated prompts for the same medical note template and measure field-level agreement. Accept if field-level accuracy >= 95% across runs.
- Probe D — KV/prefix cache effectiveness: repeated conversational steps that reuse prefix; expect cache hit rate > 60% and cost reduction > 20% over cold runs.

What Redwood can provide now:
- A self-contained probe runbook (attached) and a measurement harness you can run in your sandbox.
- A hosted parity run we can run in our region if you prefer to avoid provisioning VMs (requires anonymized sample dataset and an S3 read-only bucket).
- Shortlist of config knobs we plan to test: batching window, kv_cache_ttl, quantization profile, and fallback routing rules.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) You share the RFQ criteria spreadsheet and any sample prompts/datasets (you mentioned one earlier).
2) We prepare a probe run plan and a short script to run locally (2 business days).
3) Schedule a 45-minute follow-up to walk through results and parity matrix (propose Tue 10/12 or Wed 10/13).

If this matches your expectations, please reply with the dataset link and preferred test mode (redwood-hosted vs MedSync-run).

Thanks — happy to adjust probes to align with your procurement checklist.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Subject: Probe plan + runnable checklist (redwood-probe-runbook)

Hi Samantha —

Attaching the runbook and a short PoC config template (poc-config-template.yml). Below are the concrete steps we suggest so your SREs can run the probes without extra coordination:

Run modes (pick one):
- MedSync-run (preferred): you run the harness in your sandbox against the three vendor endpoints. We provide the harness and pass/fail criteria.
- Redwood-hosted: we run parity probes in our hosted infra using an anonymized sample set (requires read-only S3 access or upload to Drive).

Minimum deliverables we need from you:
- RFQ spreadsheet (final version) — to map weighting to probe pass/fail.
- One anonymized dataset (100–200 transcripts) — for structured extraction and cache tests.
- An endpoint or ingress test key for each competing vendor OR permission to use vendor endpoints in our hosted parity (your choice).

Concrete probe commands (examples are in the runbook):
- ./run_probe --mode long-context --prompt-set sampleA.json --concurrency 1 --out results/long-context.json
- ./run_probe --mode concurrency-ramp --concurrency 32 --ramp 1m --out results/conc-32.json

Expected timeline (if we get artifacts tomorrow):
- Day 0–1: confirm config, upload artifacts, and smoke test harness
- Day 2: run parity probes (Redwood-hosted can finish within 24 hours; MedSync-run depends on your infra)
- Day 3: deliver parity matrix and raw traces; schedule readout

I also attached a sanitized SOC2 snapshot per your ask (SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf) and a small example of the per-request audit schema (see runbook, section 4). If you want, Karthik (copied) can join a quick call to help wire the S3 permissions — he’s on standby.

Let us know whether you prefer Redwood-hosted runs or to run the harness yourselves.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments included: redwood-probe-runbook.pdf, SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf, poc-config-template.yml
